title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and spent about six months in jail after police in Fargo, North Dakota wrongly charged her with bank theft. She was held for nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. The charges, four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft, were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee when the fraud occurred. She was released on Christmas Eve with no way home.

Lipps is suing the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck for $10 million. Her federal lawsuit says investigators relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and surveillance video, then requested an arrest warrant without enough probable cause or further investigation. It also claims Fargo police lacked proper policies and training for facial recognition technology. Lipps lost her home, car, and personal property, and was denied medications and dentures while in custody. The city declined to comment.
